subject: Re: Security sign-off needed: Marketplace Security Packet v0.9 (AWS/GCP) + evidence sharing/disclaimers
body:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 10, 2025 at 9:14 AM
Subject: Security sign-off needed: Marketplace Security Packet v0.9 (AWS/GCP) + evidence sharing/disclaimers
Attachments: Redwood_Marketplace_Security_Packet_v0.9.pdf; Marketplace_Security_Evidence_Index_v3.xlsx; Architecture_Security_Overview_Redacted.png

Hi Aisha,

Requesting Security sign-off on the attached Marketplace Security Packet (v0.9) and the evidence index so we can submit to AWS/GCP this week.

Two specific areas we need guidance/approval on:
1) What evidence we are allowed to share with AWS/GCP reviewers (and under what conditions / NDA requirements).
2) Required disclaimers in the packet + listing FAQ so we don’t over-claim (SOC 2 / ISO posture, retention, residency, audit logs).

For context, AWS is asking for “security documentation supporting encryption, logging, and compliance posture,” and wants us to attach what we can directly in the partner portal.

Target: approval (or required edits) by EOD Wed so Partnerships can submit Thurs.

Thanks,
Soojin

—
Soojin Lee
Product Marketing Lead, Redwood Inference


---------- Forwarded message ----------
From: AWS Marketplace Security Review <aws-marketplace-security@amazon.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 7, 2025 at 4:22 PM
Subject: Redwood Inference listing submission - Security documentation request
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>

Hello,

For the security portion of the listing review, please provide documentation/evidence covering:
- Encryption in transit and at rest
- Key management (KMS/CMEK if applicable)
- Audit logging and access controls
- Data retention and data residency (by region, if applicable)
- Compliance posture (SOC 2 / ISO, if applicable)

If sharing third-party reports, please indicate any restrictions and how the reports can be provided securely.

Thank you,
AWS Marketplace Security Review

From: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 10, 2025 at 12:03 PM
Subject: Re: Security sign-off needed: Marketplace Security Packet v0.9 (AWS/GCP) + evidence sharing/disclaimers

Thanks. I reviewed v0.9.

Blocking edits needed before I can sign off (mostly wording/claims):

A) Compliance language
- Please remove “ISO 27001 certified” (we should not claim certification in the packet or listing). Use “security program aligned to ISO 27001 controls” ONLY if we add the standard disclaimer that this is not a certification.
- SOC 2: OK to say we have a SOC 2 Type II report, but add: “Report available under NDA upon request.” Do not attach the full report to a marketplace portal or email.

B) Data retention / data usage
- The packet currently reads as if “no customer data is retained.” That’s not accurate across all modes.
- We need consistent, precise language:
  - “Customer content is not used to train Redwood models.” (OK)
  - “Retention depends on configuration and deployment mode.” (Required)
  - “Default retention windows” should be stated carefully and must match actual control plane settings.

C) Audit logging
- Don’t say “all customer activity is fully audited.” Instead, specify what we log (admin/auth/entitlement events, console actions, API access logs where enabled) and note that application-level logging is customer-controlled.

D) Evidence sharing policy
- Allowed to share:
  - Pen test attestation letter / executive summary (no raw findings or full report)
  - SOC 2 bridge letter
  - Architecture diagram (redacted)
  - High-level security overview (this packet)
- Not allowed to share broadly:
  - Full SOC 2 report via marketplace attachment. Must be via secure channel with NDA.

Please route the updated doc back here and I’ll confirm sign-off.

-Aisha

Dr. Aisha Rahman
VP Security, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 10, 2025 at 2:18 PM
Subject: Re: Security sign-off needed: Marketplace Security Packet v0.9 (AWS/GCP) + evidence sharing/disclaimers

+1 to Aisha’s notes. A few technical corrections to keep us out of trouble with reviewers:

1) Encryption / KMS wording
- Packet says “customer-managed keys supported for all deployments.” That’s not accurate.
- Suggest: “Encryption at rest uses cloud-provider key management (AWS KMS / GCP KMS). Customer-managed keys are supported for Redwood Private deployments and select Dedicated configurations (subject to availability).”

2) Audit logs
- We can confidently claim we generate audit logs for control plane + security-relevant events (org admin changes, SSO config changes, API key events, marketplace entitlement events, and admin access).
- We should NOT imply we log/model every prompt/response. If we talk about request logging, phrase it as “configurable” and “customer-controlled.”

3) “No prompt storage”
- The current language is too absolute. We should say:
  - “Redwood does not use customer prompts/responses to train models.”
  - “Prompt/response retention (if enabled) is limited and configurable; enterprise customers may request reduced retention.”
(We should verify the default value before we put a number in the packet.)

If Soojin wants, I can drop exact replacement text for Sections 3–5.

Marcus

Marcus Lin
Security Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, Feb 11, 2025 at 9:06 AM
Subject: Re: Security sign-off needed: Marketplace Security Packet v0.9 (AWS/GCP) + evidence sharing/disclaimers

Adding the GRC perspective on evidence handling:

SOC 2 handling (required):
- We can state “SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA” in the packet.
- We should not upload the SOC 2 report to AWS/GCP portals. Those attachments are too easy to propagate.
- If AWS/GCP insists on “attaching a report,” we can attach the bridge letter + a short “SOC 2 availability statement” instead, and offer a secure download link after NDA.

Pen test handling:
- Attestation letter/executive summary only. No vulnerability details.

Evidence index:
- The attached index (v3) already has owners + refresh cadence. Please keep the “Distribution Restrictions” column in the version we send internally.

If needed, I can provide a one-paragraph boilerplate disclaimer for the packet:
“Certain reports are confidential and shared only under NDA and subject to Redwood’s report distribution policy.”

Olga

Olga Petrov
GRC Lead, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Security sign-off needed: Marketplace Security Packet v0.9 (AWS/GCP) + evidence sharing/disclaimers
Attachments: Redwood_Marketplace_Security_Packet_v0.9.1.pdf; SOC2_Bridge_Letter_2025Q1.pdf; PenTest_Attestation_Letter_2024.pdf

Thanks all — incorporated the blocking edits and re-exported as v0.9.1.

Changes made:
- Removed “ISO 27001 certified” and replaced with “aligned with industry standard frameworks (e.g., ISO 27001)” + added “not a certification” disclaimer.
- SOC 2 wording updated to “SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA upon request.”
- Rewrote retention section to avoid absolutes and added “varies by deployment mode and configuration.” (Still need final confirmation on whether we should include any default # of days; currently it does NOT specify a number.)
- Audit logging section now lists what we log (admin/control plane) and calls out optionality for request logging.
- Added a “Report distribution policy” paragraph per Olga.

Two remaining decisions for sign-off:
1) Is it OK to attach bridge letter + pen test attestation + redacted architecture diagram directly in AWS portal? (Per Aisha’s earlier note, sounds yes.)
2) Do we want to state explicit retention defaults anywhere (30/7/etc) or keep it qualitative in marketplace materials?

If you can confirm (1) + (2), we’re ready to proceed.

Soojin

Date: Tue, Feb 11, 2025 at 2:29 PM
Subject: Re: Security sign-off needed: Marketplace Security Packet v0.9 (AWS/GCP) + evidence sharing/disclaimers

On (2): I strongly recommend we avoid hard-coded retention defaults in a marketplace packet unless SecEng confirms they are stable across product + modes.

If we need to say something for buyers, we can use:
- “Retention is configurable. Customers may request reduced retention and/or configure log retention based on their requirements.”
- “Redwood does not use customer content for training.”

Separately: what’s our approved phrasing for “EU data residency” for the marketplace listing? We’ve had EMEA prospects ask for it.

Naomi

Naomi Feldman
PM, Security & Compliance Requirements

Date: Tue, Feb 11, 2025 at 3:11 PM
Subject: Re: Security sign-off needed: Marketplace Security Packet v0.9 (AWS/GCP) + evidence sharing/disclaimers

Answers + sign-off conditions:

(1) AWS portal attachments
Approved to attach:
- SOC2 bridge letter
- Pen test attestation letter (or executive summary if it’s high-level)
- Redacted architecture/security overview diagram
- The security packet itself

Not approved to attach:
- Full SOC 2 report
- Full pen test report

(2) Retention defaults
Agree with Naomi: do not include numeric defaults in marketplace collateral unless we lock them down and can maintain them. Keep it qualitative and configuration-based.

EU residency phrasing
Use: “Redwood supports regional deployments. Data is processed and stored in the selected region(s) associated with your deployment, subject to service availability. EU regions are available for eligible plans. Contact Redwood for region availability and residency requirements.”

Also, please make sure the packet/listing avoid:
- “HIPAA compliant” / “PCI compliant” claims (unless Legal + Security have explicitly approved for a specific offering). Safer: “supports requirements” / “can be configured to support.”
- “customer-managed keys for all deployments” (Marcus already flagged)
- Any absolute language like “no data ever stored/logged.”

With those conditions met, I’m OK to proceed with v0.9.1.

-Aisha

And we’ll keep the “SOC 2 report available under NDA” path as an off-portal process (secure channel) only.

One more operational question: for tracking/chain-of-custody, is there a preferred method for sharing the SOC 2 report when requested (e.g., secure portal only; named recipients)?

Soojin

From: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 13, 2025 at 5:38 PM
Subject: Re: Security sign-off needed: Marketplace Security Packet v0.9 (AWS/GCP) + evidence sharing/disclaimers

Yes — SOC 2 report distribution must follow our standard process:

- NDA executed (or existing NDA confirmed).
- Share via secure portal/link with expiration.
- Named recipients only (no broad alias lists), and we keep a record of:
  - company
  - recipients
  - date shared
  - version period of report

Olga can help coordinate the mechanics/logging; please do not email the SOC 2 report as an attachment.

Thanks for tightening the language here. Proceed.

-Aisha
